reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is framed as a fan-made entertainment production featuring voice actors dubbing Sonic 06 dialogue over game footage. Its credits support a production and attribution context, while the optional Patreon request does not describe an investment return, payment requirement, credential request, deceptive claim, or transaction outcome.

citations.quote: Sonic the Hedgehog (2006) | Real-Time Fandub Games
A group of voice actors dub the dialogue from Sonic 06... in one take... with zero rehearsal.
I have a Patreon for those who would be interested in supporting me financially!
Game footage provided by Windii
"Real-Time Fandub" originally created by Charley Marlowe

opening.argument: The description pairs a direct request for viewers to provide financial support with a dedicated Patreon destination. That is a solicitation: viewers are asked to move from watching the entertainment content to an external payment-support channel. The material does not explain what supporters receive, what funds accomplish, or what safeguards apply. That missing transaction context makes the financial ask difficult to evaluate and supports treating the video as a low-barrier monetization funnel rather than purely incidental entertainment.

citations.quote: I have a Patreon for those who would be interested in supporting me financially!
https://www.patreon.com/SnapCube

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the production fan-made does not answer the separate financial solicitation. The credits and dubbing description establish how the video was made, but they do not establish that the Patreon request is harmless, transparent, or unrelated to the viewer's decision to engage. The request is placed alongside the video’s promotional information and is paired with an external payment page.

citations.quote: A group of voice actors dub the dialogue from Sonic 06... in one take... with zero rehearsal.
I have a Patreon for those who would be interested in supporting me financially!
https://www.patreon.com/SnapCube

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The request asks only for optional financial support; it does not promise a reward, return, withdrawal, or asset. A Patreon URL alone does not establish a scam, and the description identifies the video as a voice-acting production with credits. The argument supplies no evidence that viewers must pay or that the page misrepresents what support provides.

citations.quote: I have a Patreon for those who would be interested in supporting me financially!
A group of voice actors dub the dialogue from Sonic 06... in one take... with zero rehearsal.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an explicit financial-support appeal, a Patreon link, and numerous additional external links directing viewers to social, video, music, and creator pages. The volume of outbound destinations makes the description function as a traffic-and-monetization hub, while the financial request is not accompanied by terms, a defined benefit, or a clear explanation of the transaction. A careful reviewer should therefore treat the solicitation as potentially deceptive rather than assuming the entertainment framing resolves the risk.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The production credits do not neutralize the combination of an explicit financial appeal and an external Patreon destination. Describing the content as a fandub explains the entertainment wrapper, but the description also advertises existing patrons and multiple off-platform destinations. That combination is precisely why the financial component deserves scrutiny rather than being dismissed as incidental.

citations.quote: I have a Patreon for those who would be interested in supporting me financially!
Special thanks to my already existing Patrons!
https://www.patreon.com/SnapCube

true_side_reply.rebuttal: External links are not inherently deceptive, and the listed links are consistent with cast, music, footage, and channel attribution. The only financial language is an optional request for support; there is no return claim, urgency, false testimonial, credential request, or required payment. The risk argument turns ordinary credits and social links into evidence they do not provide.

opening.argument: Although the video presents itself as entertainment, its surrounding description also performs promotional work: it invites financial support, highlights existing patrons, and directs viewers to a Patreon page and the creator’s channels. The entertainment is therefore not the only relevant function. It supplies attention that can be converted into participation in an external support program, while the description gives no concrete account of what that participation delivers. The promotional framing supports classifying the content as a solicitation with insufficiently clear terms.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title and credits may describe the visible format, but they do not eliminate the promotional function of the description. The financial-support request is explicit, and the creator supplies a Patreon destination. The fact that the video uses game footage and voice actors can explain why viewers arrive; it does not show that the resulting solicitation is adequately disclosed or limited to noncommercial entertainment.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The entertainment framing is not merely a cover: the title identifies a real-time fandub, and the description explains the voice-acting format, credits the footage provider, and identifies the original format creator. Asking interested viewers to support the creator does not become a scam simply because it appears beside entertainment. Nothing states a guaranteed benefit or conceals a payment condition.
